response: Look at what decades of failed socialist stagnation have brought to Cuba—a nation now tottering toward a desperate political transition. The tragic reality of absolute state control is that the hardworking people on the ground own nothing and have been reduced to impoverishment, stripped of personal responsibility and the chance to build generational security. And who is waiting in the wings to capitalize on this breakdown of social order? A wealthy diaspora and foreign investors ready to swoop in and buy up property and businesses at bargain prices, sweeping aside the cultural continuity of the homeland. This is what happens when traditional bonds and stable, orderly governance are eroded by radical experiments. Without a firm grounding in property ownership and true self-reliance, the local population is left entirely vulnerable to outside economic forces.
